transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is I keep getting stuck on how my jaw and one side of my face look. It seems kind of sagging and uneven to me, especially after I saw myself in a bunch of family photos. My wife and even clients say they barely notice anything, but I keep focusing on it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to try to fix or check how your jaw or face looks, like touching it, adjusting your posture, or checking mirrors often?

Yeah, I do. Before I meet with clients I’ll usually check the bathroom mirror, and then I’ll check my phone camera too, sometimes a few times. I mess with the lighting or turn my face different ways to see if it looks better.

I’ll also adjust my collar or try to hold my jaw a certain way. And if I’m at a gallery event or around other advisors, I catch myself comparing my face to theirs, especially younger guys, instead of just paying attention to the conversation.
Do these concerns about your face ever get in the way of your work, relationships, or other areas of your life, or cause you a lot of upset even when others reassure you?

Yeah, it does get in the way some. I mean, I still do my job and I show up, but I’ve been slower getting out the door for client meetings because I’m checking how I look or trying to get comfortable with it.

And during some appointments, I’m not as present as I should be. Part of my mind is on whether they’re noticing my face. I’ve also skipped a few art openings because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. So it’s not stopping my whole life, but it is affecting things.
When you’re worried about how your face looks during meetings or events, do you feel anxious that others are judging you or thinking negatively about your appearance?

Yeah, I do worry they’re seeing it. It’s mostly that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. Ever since I noticed it in those family photos, I keep thinking other people can see it too, even when my wife or clients say they barely notice anything.
Do you believe that the unevenness or sagging on one side of your face is a defect that makes you look abnormal or unattractive?

Yeah… I do. I know other people say they barely notice it, but to me it looks like a real flaw. Like one side of my jaw and face is sagging or uneven, and once I saw it in those family photos, I kind of got stuck on it. It makes me feel like I look older or unattractive, even if my wife or clients tell me it’s not obvious.
When you look in the mirror or see photos of yourself, do you see the unevenness or sagging as a major flaw that others should notice, even if they tell you they don't?

Yeah… that’s pretty much what brings me in. When I look in the mirror or see photos, I get stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. It feels really obvious to me, even though my wife and even clients have said they barely notice anything.

When you look at your face and focus on the unevenness or sagging, do you believe there is something visibly wrong that others should also see, or do you feel like it's something only you notice and worry about?

I guess it feels like there is something visibly wrong, yeah. I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. It really stood out to me after seeing myself in those family photos. Even though my wife and clients say they barely notice it, I still feel like it’s there and that other people should be able to see it too.
How much time per day would you say you spend thinking about or checking the way your jaw and face look?

Probably more than I’d like to admit. I get stuck thinking about that sagging or uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, especially since seeing those family photos. It comes up a lot during the day, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice it.
Can you give me a more specific estimate of how much time you spend each day thinking about or checking how your jaw and face look?

It’s hard to put an exact number on it, but probably an hour or two total on a normal day. Before client meetings I’ll check the bathroom mirror and then my phone camera several times, adjust the lighting, maybe change my collar or angle my face a certain way. And then at events or meetings, I catch myself comparing my face to younger advisors or people there instead of just focusing on the conversation.

When you see the sagging or uneven look on one side of your face, have you ever wondered if it might be related to a medical condition like a stroke or nerve problem, or have you had medical evaluations to check for that?

I’m not really sure. I’ve wondered in a vague way if something could be off, but I haven’t really had a medical evaluation for a stroke or nerve problem specifically. It’s more that I see it and get bothered by how it looks.

Do you believe that this uneven or sagging look on one side of your face makes you look physically abnormal or disfigured, or is it more about the symmetry not being perfect even if it doesn’t make you look noticeably flawed?

I don’t know that I’d say disfigured, exactly. It’s more that when I see it, especially in photos, I get stuck on how saggy or uneven my jaw and one side of my face look. To me it stands out a lot, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything.
Do you feel that your concern about your face is excessive or unreasonable, even though others don't seem to notice it or agree that it's a problem?

Yeah, I mean… part of me knows it’s probably more than other people see. My wife and even clients say they barely notice anything, so I can tell I’m getting stuck on it more than makes sense.

But when I look at photos, especially those family photos, I really see this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, and it’s hard to let it go.

When you look at your face and focus on the sagging or uneven appearance, would you say that the issue is something that most people would consider minor or barely noticeable, or do you feel that it’s something more significant that others should also see as a clear flaw?

I guess most people would probably see it as minor, if they notice it at all. My wife and clients say they barely see anything. But for me, I keep getting stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face, especially after those family photos. It just stands out to me.
